name: tweet-grid

frames.best_why: All six cards are fully in view with no cursor over any text.

tagline: Three-column wall of tweet cards in a staggered masonry layout.
summary: A responsive masonry grid of tweet-style cards, each with author, handle, body, date and reply, repost and like counts.
appearance: Six dark rounded tweet cards sit in three staggered columns, each with a round avatar, bold name, grey handle, small X mark, a few lines of text, a date and a row of emoji counts.
behaviour: Static: nothing moves or responds beyond a faint border shift on hover.
demo_content: Six invented tweets from Maya Chen, Diego Alvarez, Priya Raman, Tom Becker, Aisha Bello and Lucas Moreau.
search_phrases: wall of tweets in three columns
customer love wall for a landing page
use_when: You want a dense wall of short social-style quotes with author photos and engagement counts.
avoid_when: You need live posts; these are static mock cards with no network fetch.
customise: tweets takes inline objects with name, handle, avatar, text and counts, and columns and spacing are props; card styling is fixed in the source.
weight_why: Static cards with a single CSS border transition.

a11y.note: Cards are not interactive; avatars use the name as alt, but counts are emoji plus digits with no text labels for screen readers.

issues: Reply, repost and like counts are emoji plus digits with no text label.
Cards are not links or buttons, so nothing in the wall is interactive.
polish_why: Clean masonry and believable cards, but standard bordered tiles with little distinction.
